verdict.root_cause: An automated change harness set cartservice's REDIS_ADDR to redis-cart:6380 (a non-default Redis port, from an unset state) about two minutes before onset, and unlike four prior cycles of the same experiment this edit was never reverted [tr_919214de917a]. cartservice's Redis connection to redis-cart:6380 never completes, and because the cart store's connection check runs in the startup path from the program entry point, the unhandled exception kills the process; it crash-loops roughly every second from ~13:39:20 [tr_44eefec950d0]. With no cart listener, every checkoutservice PlaceOrder aborts at the outbound hipstershop.CartService/GetCart leaf — the deepest error-bearing span, failing in under 1ms — and the ERROR propagates to the frontend HTTP root, explaining the simultaneous checkoutservice/frontend/loadgenerator alerts [tr_5643554a7104]. checkoutservice itself is healthy and unchanged [tr_bb8b9d08b3a8, tr_58d24c8ac46e].
verdict.reasoning: The mechanism is a config value that is itself wrong: the address cartservice is told to dial. The logged connection string names redis-cart:6380 against a 6379 default, and that value arrived via an env edit two minutes pre-onset [tr_919214de917a, tr_44eefec950d0]. Not resource_exhaustion — the process exits on its own application exception, not an external kill. Not dependency_latency — checkout traces complete in under 3ms with the cart hop under 1ms [tr_5643554a7104]. Not bad_deploy — the hotfix image was reverted ~30 minutes before onset, so the running artifact is the intended one [tr_919214de917a]. Direction is settled by trace shape: the error originates at the GetCart leaf, checkoutservice's own spans carry 0.1-0.2ms self time and the intermediate span is not ERROR, and checkoutservice has an empty change record [tr_5643554a7104, tr_58d24c8ac46e]. Reverting REDIS_ADDR is the fix; a restart alone re-enters the loop.
open_questions: No one queried the redis-cart service definition, so it is inferred rather than confirmed that redis-cart listens on 6379 and not 6380 [tr_44eefec950d0 rates this low].

The 20-45s hang before each failure is timeout-shaped, not the fast refusal a wrong-port dial to a live host usually gives [tr_44eefec950d0]; redis-cart was never dispatched on, and it may also be unreachable or dropping packets on 6380.

cartservice has no Prometheus series over 12 hours and checkoutservice's error-ratio baseline covers 01:40-07:40Z, excluding onset, so blast radius and the exact crash-loop start rest entirely on logs [tr_b5e85f0cad3f, tr_ef7813a3e1e6].

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself is down or not accepting connections, so cartservice would crash-loop regardless of the dialed port.
alternatives.why_not: Never dispatched on, so unfalsified rather than supported; timing favours the env edit, since four identical prior edits were reverted before they could bite [tr_919214de917a]. The timeout-shaped delays are the one observation keeping it alive [tr_44eefec950d0].

alternatives.root_cause: A checkoutservice change landing shortly before 13:40:45 broke the cart call path.
alternatives.why_not: The change query started at onset so a just-prior edit would be missed, but checkoutservice's spans are error-free at its own layers and cart is demonstrably crash-looping independently [tr_58d24c8ac46e, tr_5643554a7104, tr_44eefec950d0].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring cartservice's pre-13:38:07 environment (REDIS_ADDR unset / image default) and recreating it should end the startup crash loop: in Loki {service="cart-service"} the repeating Redis-connect + unhandled ApplicationException pair naming redis-cart:6380 stops and normal GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync lines resume; in Tempo the checkoutservice/hipstershop.CartService/GetCart leaf stops carrying ERROR and PlaceOrder traces reach payment/shipping/email spans; checkoutservice logs regain the full order lifecycle lines. Confirmation must come from logs and traces, as cartservice has no Prometheus calls_total series.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if cartservice still crashes on startup after the recreate — naming 6380 (revert did not take) or 6379 (port was never the fault and redis-cart is itself down or dropping packets; its listening port is inferred, not confirmed). Also falsified if cartservice comes up clean but GetCart spans stay ERROR.
proposal.risk: If redis-cart is unreachable regardless of port, this fixes nothing and destroys the only live artefact of the harness edit. The prior state is recorded as unset rather than known-good, so the restored default could itself be wrong and the crash loop continues. The harness has re-applied this edit on a ~4.5h cycle four times, so the incident can recur; stopping it is outside this system.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice only. Callers frontend and checkoutservice see a connection reset during recreate, indistinguishable from the failure they already have; redis-cart sees cart traffic move off 6380. Downstream checkout stages resume receiving traffic once orders pass the cart hop.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts hit checkout and frontend simultaneously with user-facing impact and no open incident to fold into. The simultaneous onset across the checkout path suggests a shared dependency or a deploy, but nothing in the alerts picks between them.
